newsitem.title: USA: Virginia budget plans would boost state worker pay.
newsitem.headline: Virginia budget plans would boost state worker pay.

text.p: Virginia's House and Senate approved separate versions of a $35 billion, two-year budget that raises state employees' pay and adds 1,100 new police officers.
A conference committee will begin working out a compromise next week on the plans, which revise the second half of the biennial budget adopted last year.
The General Assembly is scheduled to end its annual session on Feb 22.

Both plans added about $60 million in spending to the budget released in December by Gov. George Allen, who proposed allocating $226 million of surplus funds. Both plans use most of the new cash for employee raises.
The House plan would raise state worker pay by three percent and teacher pay by four percent. The Senate version would raise state worker pay by four percent and teacher pay three percent.
The Senate agreed with Allen's proposal to spend $11 million to clean up Chesapeake Bay, while the House proposed spending $15 million on the cleanup.
Both chambers rejected Allen's proposal that the state apply for $30 million in federal money to establish charter schools.
Both approved $27 million of appropriations to shore up the state health insurance program, which could face insolvency next year. Allen recommended adding $20 million to the program.
The lawmakers cut Allen's prison building programs, proposing that the savings be used to hire 1,000 more police officers.
Allen told the Richmond Times-Dispatch that the plans were "in pretty good shape on essential matters I care about most, education, law enforcement and economic development."
